chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent an army to Khatham. When they surrounded them, they sought protection by prostrating (saying 'Sujud'). He killed some of them. When this reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said: 'Give the heirs half the blood money for their prayer (prostration).'
And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Behold, I am free from every Muslim who descends (enters) with a polytheist in the abode of war.'

key_terms.السُّجُود: Prostration (used here as a form of ritual submission/surrender)
key_terms.دَارُ الْحَرْبِ: Abode of war (territory of non-Muslims or battlefield context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on blood money for those who surrender by prostrating in battle?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) clarifies the ruling on soldiers who surrendered to polytheists in the 'abode of war' (Dar al-Harb) by performing prostration, a gesture of ritual submission. He decreed they receive half the blood money, indicating their partial status as Muslims due to their prayer, while also declaring his innocence from any Muslim who dwells among polytheists in a land of conflict. This incident highlights the juristic distinction between mere presence in enemy territory and active participation in their religious rites, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of prayer and status of the faithful in non-Muslim lands.
